LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard Arch Linux packaging practices. The source is fetched from the project's own GitHub repository via a signed git tag (`git+https://github.com/KiefStudioMA/ks-aur-scanner.git#tag=v$pkgver?signed`), with PGP key verification (`validpgpkeys`) and `sha256sums=('SKIP')` intentionally set — the maintainer explains that signature verification is stronger than hashing a GitHub-generated tarball. The `SKIP` checksum is required for VCS sources and is not a security concern.

The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `check()` functions perform routine operations: `cargo fetch` to lock dependency versions, `cargo build` to compile, and `cargo test` to run tests. The `package()` function installs binaries, shell integration scripts, a rules example, a documented pacman hook (as an opt-in example, not auto-enabled), and license/docs files — all standard staging into `$pkgdir`. There are no `curl|bash` patterns, no `eval` of decoded blobs, no unexpected network downloads, and no code that exfiltrates data or modifies system files outside the package's scope.

The integration scripts (`integration.bash`, `integration.zsh`, etc.) are sourced by users into their shell RC files to scan AUR packages before building — this is the intended functionality of a scanner tool and poses no supply-chain risk. The pacman hook is installed as `.hook.example` with an explicit note that it is "NOT auto-enabled" and that shell integration is preferred. No upstream behavior is injected that serves purposes other than the application's stated goal of scanning AUR packages.
</details>

Legitimate AUR security scanner with standard packaging, PGP-verified git source, and SKIP checksum justified by signature verification.

</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard Rust package built with Cargo. The source is fetched via `git+https` over HTTPS from the project's own upstream repository (github.com/KiefStudioMA/ks-aur-scanner), pinned to a specific GPG-signed tag (`v$pkgver`), with `validpgpkeys` configured so makepkg verifies the tag signature. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` entry is correct and required for VCS sources — per the audit guidelines, this is not a security issue.

The build pipeline uses standard Cargo commands (`cargo fetch`, `cargo build --release --locked`, `cargo test --locked`) and installs only binaries, shell-integration scripts, shell completions, rule files, and documentation into `$pkgdir` with standard permissions. The pacman hook is explicitly shipped as an opt-in example file (`aur-scan.hook.example`), not auto-enabled. No curl/wget of arbitrary scripts, no `eval` or base64 decoding, no credential or key exfiltration, and no reverse shells are present.

The shell integration scripts and pacman hook are opt-in additions that support the scanner's stated purpose (scanning AUR packages before install); they are documented and not auto-registered. Overall this deviates from no packaging standard and shows no evidence of injected malicious code.
</details>
<evidence>
